summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Harvard and Oxford, he completed his doctoral studies under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as Administrative Director at Harvard (1980–1991) and Associate Professor of Religion at Boston University (1990–2024).

Mallica Kumbera Landrus works in Indology and history and archaeology. Attested in 2026, she has served as Keeper of Eastern Art and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology, affiliated with Wolfson College and the University of Oxford.
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar. She completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ichisada Miyazaki at Kyoto University (Litt.D. 1987). He held multiple posts at Kyoto University from 1965 to 2001 and served as professor at Otani University in 2003.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society. He was also affiliated with Jadavpur University as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit (attested 2003).

Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a PhD student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. Attested in 2026, she studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a Research Scholar or Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mandan Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who held posts at the University of Rajasthan, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University as Principal and Chief Editor (~1962–1977), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as Vice-Chancellor (~1989–1996).

Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He served as full professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller and was appointed Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig in 1991.

Mangal Deva Shastri was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from approximately 1937 to 1945.

Manik Man Bajracharya works in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has held posts at the Lotus Research Centre, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018), Documenta Nepalica (attested 2018), and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).

Manlio Iofrida is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1970–1975). He later held academic posts at the University of Pisa and the University of Bologna (~1992).

Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Ernest Fenollosa at the University of Tokyo and under Mokurai Takeda. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University from 1901 to 1902.
Manu Leumann was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein worked in archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning a PhD from Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College (1888–1899) and Archaeological Surveyor and Superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of India (1904–1912).
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2016 under the doctoral supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and studied under Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen was a linguistics scholar who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1911–1954), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1911–1954), and the publication L'Humanité (~1944–1974).

Marcel Granet was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held professorships at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1920–1940) and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (~1927–1940).
